    Get started

    Get started

    Copilot can help you write, summarize, research, analyze and automate. Follow these five steps to get started at Contoso.

    1. Find out which Copilot you have

    Everyone with a Contoso work account can use Copilot Chat. With a Microsoft 365 Copilot license you also get Microsoft Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and Teams, plus the Researcher and Analyst agents. Compare the tools or request a license.

    2. Learn the basics

    Start with Build foundational generative AI skills on Microsoft Learn, then choose the track for your role in Guided learning.

    3. Try prompts that work

    Copy and adapt a reviewed prompt from the Prompt library. Say what you want, give context, and describe the format you need.

    4. Use Copilot responsibly

    Read Copilot at Contoso and our AI policy. Always check Copilot's output before you use it or share it.

    5. Get help and keep learning

    Join office hours, ask the Copilot community, or contact support.

    Copilot tools

    Which Copilot should I use?

    Contoso uses several Copilot tools. They share a name but do different jobs. Use this page to choose the right one; each name links to a page with more detail.

    Quick guide: I want to…

    • Ask a question, draft or rewrite something, or search the web: Copilot Chat
    • Work with my own email, meetings, chats and files: Microsoft Copilot
    • Get a researched report with citations: Researcher
    • Analyze data across spreadsheets and files: Analyst
    • Reuse the same instructions and knowledge for a task, or share them with my team: an agent
    • Build an agent that takes actions in business systems or serves many people: Copilot Studio
    • Build AI into an application with code and the model of my choice: Microsoft Foundry
    • Write, review or fix code: GitHub Copilot

    Side by side

    Building an agent? Pick the right tool

    • Agent Builder (in Copilot): describe the agent in plain language and ground it in files, sites or web content. Best for personal and team agents. No code.
    • Copilot Studio: design conversations, actions and workflows, connect to business systems and publish to many channels, governed by environments and data policies. Low-code.
    • Microsoft Foundry: full control of models, tools, evaluation and hosting in Azure. Pro-code.

    Microsoft guidance: Choose between Agent Builder and Copilot Studio. Before you share any agent widely, follow Agent lifecycle & approval.

    Good to know

    • New names. Microsoft 365 Copilot is now called Microsoft Copilot, and Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat is now Microsoft Copilot Chat. Licenses and admin settings may still use the older names. Azure AI Foundry is now Microsoft Foundry.
    • What we provide. Which tools and licenses are available depends on Contoso's agreements. See Request a Copilot license.
    • Same rules everywhere. Every tool follows Copilot at Contoso and our data protection controls.
    • Checked September 2026. Features and licensing change often, so follow the links on each tool's page for current details.

    Copilot tools

    Copilot Chat

    Copilot Chat (Microsoft Copilot Chat, formerly Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat) is a secure AI chat assistant for everyone with a Contoso work account. It answers from the web and from content you give it, and it runs under enterprise data protection.

    Use it for

    • Drafting, rewriting and summarizing text
    • Quick web research with cited answers
    • Working with files you upload, paste or reference
    • Using approved agents, or building simple ones with Agent Builder

    What it works with

    The web, by default. It uses your work content when you add it (upload or paste it, or type / to reference a file), when the content is open in Outlook or Teams, and through agents that Contoso has enabled. To have Copilot work across all your email, meetings, chats and files, you need Microsoft Copilot.

    Where to find it

    The Microsoft Copilot app, Microsoft Teams, Outlook and Microsoft Edge. Sign in with your Contoso work account.

    Who can use it

    Everyone with a Contoso work account. It is included with eligible Microsoft 365 plans at no extra cost, so you don't need to request a license.

    Good to know

    • Your prompts and responses are covered by enterprise data protection: they aren't used to train the underlying models, and they're logged for audit and eDiscovery.
    • Check facts against the cited sources before you rely on them.
    • Follow Copilot at Contoso and the AI policy.

    Details checked against Microsoft documentation in September 2026. Features, names and licensing change often, so follow the links for current details. Compare tools on Which Copilot should I use?

    Microsoft Copilot

    Microsoft Copilot (formerly Microsoft 365 Copilot) is the licensed version of Copilot. It works inside Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams and OneNote and in the Microsoft Copilot app, and it can reason over your own work content, including email, meetings, chats and files.

    Use it for

    • Catching up on meetings and long email threads
    • Drafting documents, emails and presentations from your existing files
    • Analyzing data in Excel
    • Finding information across your work content, and handing deeper work to Researcher or Analyst

    What it works with

    The work content you already have permission to see (email, calendar, meetings, chats and files, through Microsoft Graph), plus the web when Contoso allows it. Copilot never shows you content you can't already open.

    Where to find it

    The Copilot button in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams and OneNote, and the Microsoft Copilot app.

    Who can use it

    People with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license (licenses keep the older name). The license also includes Researcher and Analyst and lets you build agents that extend Copilot. Request a license.

    Good to know

    • Copilot respects sensitivity labels. It can use encrypted content only when you have the right to view and extract it.
    • If Copilot shows you something you don't think you should see, the content is probably overshared. Report it.
    • You're responsible for the final result, so review everything before you send or share it.

    Details checked against Microsoft documentation in September 2026. Features, names and licensing change often, so follow the links for current details. Compare tools on Which Copilot should I use?

    Researcher

    Researcher is a reasoning agent in Microsoft Copilot. It plans and runs multi-step research across the web and the work content you can access, then gives you a structured report with citations.

    Use it for

    • Market or competitor analysis that combines web sources with internal files
    • Briefings and decision memos with citations
    • Pulling together information from email, meetings and documents
    • Reworking the same findings for different audiences

    What it works with

    The public web (when Contoso allows web search) and the files, email, meetings and chats you can access. It respects existing permissions and may ask clarifying questions before it starts.

    Where to find it

    In the Microsoft Copilot app, in the list of agents or tools, and from the Copilot pane in Word.

    Who can use it

    People with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license. Request a license.

    Tips

    • Be specific about the question, the audience and the format you want.
    • Check the cited sources before you rely on the report.
    • Use Copilot Chat for quick answers and Researcher when you need depth.

    Details checked against Microsoft documentation in September 2026. Features, names and licensing change often, so follow the links for current details. Compare tools on Which Copilot should I use?

    Analyst

    Analyst is a reasoning agent in Microsoft Copilot that works like a data analyst. It reads the spreadsheets and files you give it, works through your question step by step, and returns findings with charts, tables and citations.

    Use it for

    • Finding trends and outliers across several files
    • Comparing periods or regions
    • Forecasting
    • Analysis that spans several files (for work inside a single workbook, use Copilot in Excel)

    What it works with

    Files you provide: Excel, CSV, JSON, PDF and Word.

    Where to find it

    In the Microsoft Copilot app, in the list of agents or tools.

    Who can use it

    People with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license. Request a license.

    Tips

    • Explain the question and the decision it supports.
    • Ask Analyst to explain its method and assumptions.
    • Check the results before you share them.

    Details checked against Microsoft documentation in September 2026. Features, names and licensing change often, so follow the links for current details. Compare tools on Which Copilot should I use?

    Agents

    Agents are purpose-built helpers inside Copilot. Each one combines instructions, knowledge and actions for a specific task. You can use approved agents from the Agent Store and build simple ones yourself with Agent Builder.

    Use them for

    • Team FAQs and knowledge agents over SharePoint content
    • Repeatable tasks with fixed instructions, such as onboarding help or policy questions
    • Sharing a tested agent with colleagues
    • Microsoft and partner agents that Contoso has approved

    What they work with

    Instructions you write, public websites, SharePoint and OneDrive content, and connectors or actions that Contoso provides.

    Where to find them

    In the Microsoft Copilot app and Copilot Chat: use Agent Builder to create an agent and the Agent Store to find one. Agents approved for Contoso are listed in the Agent catalog.

    Who can use them

    • Everyone can build and use agents that rely only on instructions or the public web.
    • Agents that use shared company data need a Microsoft 365 Copilot license, or pay-as-you-go billing if Contoso's IT team has turned it on. Pay-as-you-go isn't available in GCC or GCC High.

    Before you share an agent

    • Test it with real questions, including ones it shouldn't answer.
    • Only use content your audience is allowed to see, and name an owner.
    • To share it beyond your team, follow Agent lifecycle & approval. IT reviews agent requests in the Microsoft 365 admin center and publishes approved agents to the Agent Store.

    Details checked against Microsoft documentation in September 2026. Features, names and licensing change often, so follow the links for current details. Compare tools on Which Copilot should I use?

    Copilot Studio

    Microsoft Copilot Studio is a low-code, browser-based workbench for designing, testing, publishing and managing agents and workflows. Agents built there can connect to business systems and run in Copilot, Teams, websites and other channels.

    Use it for

    • Self-service agents for employees or customers
    • Agents that take actions through connectors or flows
    • Extending Microsoft Copilot with Contoso knowledge and actions
    • Agents that start from an event or run on their own

    What it works with

    Knowledge sources such as documents, SharePoint and public websites, plus connectors, Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, other agents and HTTP requests, within the limits of Contoso's data policies.

    Where to find it

    Sign in at copilotstudio.microsoft.com. Agents can be published to Microsoft Copilot, Teams, SharePoint, websites and other channels.

    Who can use it

    Makers and developers. Usage is billed in Copilot Credits, through capacity packs or pay-as-you-go. A Microsoft 365 Copilot license covers building agents that extend Copilot. Talk to the adoption team before you start a project.

    Build it the right way

    • Build in the environment you are assigned. Production agents don't belong in the default environment. See Where agents are built.
    • Contoso's data policies decide which connectors, knowledge sources and channels an agent can use. See Data protection.
    • Package agents in solutions and move them to production through pipelines, as described in Agent lifecycle & approval.

    Details checked against Microsoft documentation in September 2026. Features, names and licensing change often, so follow the links for current details. Compare tools on Which Copilot should I use?

    Microsoft Foundry

    Microsoft Foundry (formerly Azure AI Foundry) is Azure's platform for developers to choose models, build and host AI apps and agents with low code or full code, and then test, secure and monitor them in production.

    Use it for

    • Building prompt agents, or hosted agents that run your own code
    • Choosing and deploying models from a large catalog, including Microsoft, OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta models
    • Adding tools, memory and retrieval to agents
    • Tracing, evaluating and monitoring agents

    What it works with

    The models you choose, plus the data and tools you connect through built-in tools, memory and retrieval.

    Where to find it

    The Foundry portal at ai.azure.com, SDKs for Python, C#, JavaScript and Java, the Azure Developer CLI and the Visual Studio Code extension.

    Who can use it

    Professional developers and AI engineers, through an Azure subscription. You pay for what you use. Ask for access to a Contoso subscription or Foundry project.

    Security and governance

    • Access uses Azure role-based access control with Microsoft Entra ID, including Foundry roles such as Foundry User and Foundry Owner.
    • Guardrails (formerly content filters) check model inputs and outputs.
    • The Foundry Control Plane gives an inventory of agents and their compliance status.

    Details checked against Microsoft documentation in September 2026. Features, names and licensing change often, so follow the links for current details. Compare tools on Which Copilot should I use?

    GitHub Copilot

    GitHub Copilot is an AI pair programmer and coding agent built into GitHub and popular code editors. It suggests code, answers questions about a codebase, reviews pull requests and can take on coding tasks for you to review.

    Use it for

    • Writing code faster with code completions and next edit suggestions
    • Explaining, refactoring and testing code in chat or agent mode
    • Handing an issue to the cloud agent, which opens a pull request for you to review
    • Automatic pull request reviews

    What it works with

    The code in your editor and repositories, and GitHub context such as issues and pull requests. Admins can exclude files and repositories from Copilot.

    Where to find it

    Visual Studio Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains IDEs and Xcode; GitHub.com and GitHub Mobile; the Copilot CLI; and the GitHub Copilot desktop app.

    Who can use it

    Developers with a seat assigned through Contoso's GitHub organization (Copilot Business or Copilot Enterprise). Features beyond code completions use GitHub AI Credits, which your GitHub admins budget. Request access.

    Use it responsibly

    • Review every suggestion and pull request as you would a colleague's.
    • Follow Contoso's secure development standards, and never put secrets in prompts or code.
    • Admins can block suggestions that match public code, or show them with a code reference and license.

    Details checked against GitHub documentation in September 2026. Features, names and licensing change often, so follow the links for current details. Compare tools on Which Copilot should I use?

    Tips for better prompts

    • Goal: say what you want Copilot to do.
    • Context: explain why you need it and who it's for.
    • Source: point to the files, emails or sites to use.
    • Expectations: describe the format, length and tone.

    Then refine the result: ask Copilot to shorten it, expand it, or change the tone.

    Use AI responsibly

    Copilot at Contoso

    Copilot helps you work faster, but you remain responsible for what you create and share. These principles apply to every Copilot tool at Contoso.

    Your responsibilities

    • Follow our AI policy. Read the Contoso AI policy before you start.
    • Check the output. Copilot can be wrong or incomplete. Verify facts, figures and citations before you rely on them or share them.
    • Use approved tools. Use the tools on this site, signed in with your work account, for Contoso information. Don't paste Contoso information into personal or consumer AI services.
    • Protect sensitive data. Label files and emails correctly, and never remove protection to make content easier for AI to use.
    • Share wisely. Copilot only shows content you can already access, so keep permissions on your files and sites tight. Report anything Copilot shows you that you shouldn't be able to see.
    • Be transparent. Follow Contoso guidance on disclosing AI assistance, especially in customer-facing or official content.
    • Report problems. Tell support about harmful, biased or inaccurate output.

    What Copilot can see

    Microsoft Copilot only uses organizational data that you already have permission to view. Copilot Chat works from the web and the content you give it. Prompts and responses are covered by enterprise data protection and aren't used to train the underlying models.

    Learn more: Data, privacy and security for Microsoft Copilot · Copilot Chat privacy and protections · Data protection

    Data protection for Copilot and agents

    Copilot follows the same security, compliance and privacy controls as the rest of Microsoft 365. Here are the controls that matter most, and what they mean for you.

    Permissions come first

    Copilot only surfaces content that you already have at least view access to. If it shows you something you shouldn't see, the content is overshared. Report it so the owner can fix the permissions.

    Sensitivity labels

    Label your files and emails. Copilot can use encrypted content only when you have both the view and extract rights for it.

    Data loss prevention (DLP)

    Contoso can use Microsoft Purview DLP policies for Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat to:

    • stop Copilot from using files and emails with specific sensitivity labels (they may still appear as citations)
    • block web searches when a prompt contains sensitive information
    • block prompts that contain sensitive information (preview)
    • keep external email out of Copilot's answers and summaries (preview)

    If Copilot won't use a file or answer a prompt, a policy may be protecting that information.

    Keeping sensitive sites out of Copilot

    Admins can use SharePoint Advanced Management to find and fix oversharing, with data access governance reports and site access reviews. Restricted Content Discovery hides selected sites from organization-wide search and Copilot without changing their permissions.

    Monitoring

    Copilot interactions are logged for audit and eDiscovery. Microsoft Purview Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) gives security teams one view of data risk across AI apps and agents.

    For agent builders

    Copilot Studio agents run in Power Platform environments whose data policies group connectors as Business, Non-business or Blocked. The policies can also block knowledge sources, connector tools, HTTP requests, channels and event triggers. Approved connectors lists what you can use; ask the adoption team about anything else.

    For developers

    • Microsoft Foundry: access is controlled with Azure role-based access control and Microsoft Entra ID, and guardrails check model inputs and outputs.
    • GitHub Copilot: admins set policies and models, can exclude content, and can block suggestions that match public code. Copilot activity is recorded in audit logs.

    Details checked against Microsoft documentation in September 2026. Features, names and licensing change often, so follow the links for current details. Compare tools on Which Copilot should I use?

    Agent lifecycle and approval

    Agents can reach many people quickly, so every agent shared beyond a small team follows the same lifecycle at Contoso.

    1. Plan

    Describe the problem, the audience, the data the agent needs and who will own it. Check the Agent catalog for an existing agent first, and pick the right tool on Which Copilot should I use?

    2. Build

    Use only data that your audience is allowed to see. Build Copilot Studio agents in the environment you are assigned. See Where agents are built.

    3. Test

    Try real questions, including ones the agent shouldn't answer. Check that it cites its sources and says so when it doesn't know.

    4. Submit for review

    Send the agent to the adoption team with its purpose, audience, data sources and owner. The team reviews it for value, security and ownership.

    5. Publish

    IT reviews agent requests in the Microsoft 365 admin center and publishes approved agents to the Agent Store, where they can also be assigned, blocked or removed. Copilot Studio agents move to production in solutions, through pipelines with approvals. Approved agents are added to the Agent catalog.

    6. Maintain and retire

    Owners review their agents regularly, keep content current and ask for retirement when an agent is no longer needed. The admin center's Agent Registry flags agents without owners.

    Details checked against Microsoft documentation in September 2026. Features, names and licensing change often, so follow the links for current details. Compare tools on Which Copilot should I use?

    Get started

    Request a Copilot license

    Everyone with a Contoso work account can already use Copilot Chat. You don't need to request it.

    Microsoft 365 Copilot license

    This license adds Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and Teams, Copilot that works across your email, meetings, chats and files, and the Researcher and Analyst agents. Microsoft now calls the product Microsoft Copilot, but the license keeps the Microsoft 365 Copilot name.

    1. Check Which Copilot should I use? to confirm it's the right tool for your work.
    2. We recommend completing the Everyone track in Guided learning.
    3. Submit a license request with your role and how you plan to use Copilot.

    Other Copilot tools

    • Copilot Studio: talk to the adoption team. Usage is billed in Copilot Credits.
    • Microsoft Foundry: request access to an Azure subscription or Foundry project through support.
    • GitHub Copilot: request a seat in Contoso's GitHub organization.

    Hackathons

    Hackathons

    A hackathon brings people from different teams together to build agents and Copilot solutions for real Contoso problems in a short, focused event. It's a fast way to build skills and find ideas worth scaling.

    Planning one?

    • Pick two or three business problems with clear owners.
    • Mix skills: people who know the process, makers, and a developer or IT contact.
    • Choose the tools up front (Agent Builder, Copilot Studio or Microsoft Foundry) and set up environments and data access in advance.
    • Agree how winning ideas will move through the agent lifecycle.

    Talk to the adoption team about planning a hackathon.
